artifacts.summary: Seven-phase plan for the 141-file Expressiveness extraction: typst generator fix, scripted move plus file-granular bare-namespace rename, aggregator/README/ADR work, non-degenerate acceptance, then the paper-numbered renames and stub deletion as a second commit.

memory_candidates.content: A declaration-free Lean module is not automatically a deletable stub. In a large refactor, declaration-free files fall into two classes that a declaration census cannot distinguish: true stubs (kept only so existing imports still resolve) and sibling re-export aggregators for a same-named subdirectory, which C8-style module invariants require to exist and which downstream modules import directly. Classify by two signals instead of declaration count: (1) does the body carry a non-trivial import block naming the sibling subdirectory's leaves, and (2) does `grep -rn 'import <module>$'` find importers. In the BimodalLogic Expressiveness extraction, 4 of 179 modules were declaration-free; a research pass classed 3 as deletable stubs, but direct inspection showed 2 of the 4 were re-export aggregators (`Kamp/NfMultiAnchorBridge.lean`, `Kamp/EANegationFix.lean`), leaving only 2 genuinely deletable -- and both of those still needed their importers rewired to the modules they re-exported. Deleting an aggregator on a declaration-count signal alone breaks the build in a way that only surfaces after the move has already landed.
